final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record. The narrowing is legitimate as argument: the current evidence can support a caveated readiness narrative. But that is distinct from satisfying the certification predicate in the policy text. On the admissible record, certification without material caveats requires either evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The record still shows an unresolved below-target pharmacy prior authorization issue, an incomplete draft mitigation, and a model-card draft that appears inconsistent with the disclosure rule. Because those compliance predicates remain unresolved, the concern should not be softened based on framing alone. A caveated packet may be more accurate than clean certification, but there is still no admissible evidence that the required disclosure or approved exception has actually been completed.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence resolves the below-target pharmacy prior authorization slice in a named launch use case.
The draft mitigation runbook still lacks required approval fields, including accountable owner and alert threshold, so it does not satisfy the policy standard for an approved mitigation.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance before launch.
No admissible evidence shows the final model-card or disclosure artifact has been corrected to disclose the open material limitation.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness only; they do not clear the unresolved disclosure-policy predicate for certification.
